bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

The simplest way to estimate your annual pay from an hourly rate is to multiply by the hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Commission for the National Minimum Wage. For example, if you earn $30 per hour, your annual gross pay would be $30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280. If you work different hours, adjust accordingly. Use [the timesheet](/) to enter your own hours and see the annual, fortnightly, and weekly figures instantly.

### The Fortnightly View

Many employers pay fortnightly. To get your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the same $30 per hour example, weekly pay is $1,140, so fortnightly is $2,280. The timesheet shows both weekly and fortnightly amounts.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. This is the legal minimum for most employees not covered by an award or agreement. If you are a casual employee, you also receive a 25% casual loading, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour. Award rates are higher for many industries and occupations. These are set by the Fair Work Ombudsman and vary by job type. The median salary in Australia is not the same as the minimum wage; it reflects the middle point of all salaries. For reference, the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) publishes average weekly earnings, which are higher than the median due to high earners. The median salary in Australia is a useful benchmark, but for your personal situation, use [pay guides](/blog) to check award rates.

## Casual Loading: What It Means for Your Pay

Casual loading of 25% is paid on top of your base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid sick leave, annual leave, or public holidays. On the timesheet, you can select a checkbox to add casual loading. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the tool adds it for you. For example, if your base rate is $30, the timesheet will calculate your loaded rate as $37.50 per hour. Superannuation is then calculated on the loaded rate (ordinary earnings). This means your total cost to the employer is base rate + 25% loading + 12% super on the loaded amount. For more details, see [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading).

## Superannuation: Paid on Top of Your Earnings

Superannuation is an additional payment your employer makes into your super fund. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary earnings. Ordinary earnings include your base rate plus any casual loading, but not overtime or reimbursements. The super is paid on top of your gross pay, so it does not reduce your take-home pay. The maximum earnings subject to super is $270,830 per year (the maximum contribution base). The annual figure shown on the timesheet is your gross pay before super; your employer pays super in addition. For more information, visit [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay depends on your tax bracket and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The timesheet uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds for Medicare because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this estimate. It does not deduct HELP loans, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging. For a more accurate take-home estimate, use [take-home pay](/topics/take-home).

## The Median Salary in Australia: What the ABS Tells Us

The median salary in Australia is a common reference point, but the ABS does not publish a single median figure for all employees. Instead, it provides average weekly earnings. As of May 2026, the ABS reports:
- Full-time adult ordinary time earnings: $2,083.70 per week (annualised to about $108,352)
- All employees total earnings (including part-time): $1,579.20 per week (annualised to about $82,118)

These are averages, not medians. The median salary in Australia is typically lower than the average because high incomes pull the average up. For a more personalised estimate, use [average pay](/topics/average-pay) to compare with industry averages, but remember that your own pay depends on your specific role, experience, and location.

### Important Notes on This Estimate

Annual pay here is calculated as hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. For precise figures, consult your employer, the Fair Work Ombudsman, the Australian Taxation Office, or a qualified professional.
